A.text: Resin infiltration is a measure for small noncavitated interproximal lesions in primary and permanent teeth, aimed at reducing progression.

B.text: Restoring a lesion does not by itself halt the disease process, so this rationale is incorrect.

C.text: Interim therapeutic restorations provide caries control in children with multiple open lesions before definitive restoration. This child has a single small noncavitated lesion, for which resin infiltration is the specified measure.

D.text: Not every caries lesion needs restoration, so the claim that all lesions must be restored is wrong.

explanation.text: A small noncavitated interproximal lesion in a permanent tooth can be managed with resin infiltration to reduce progression.
Restoration is not required for every lesion, and restoring does not by itself stop the disease.
